answer: Time-locked staking resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a bond in a smart-contract vault acting as an admission jetty. On each checkpoint pulse, validators audit signed task receipts and slash accounts caught equivocating or spamming. Attackers incur liquidity lockup and slashing risk per fake identity. However, steep bond floors exclude low-capital operators while letting deep-pocketed adversaries buy multiple slots.
